newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end down, unaffected by Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end down, unaffected by Deng's death.

text.p: * Index still ends above 3,300 support level
Manila shares ended a shade down on Thursday as focus on thirdliners remained and traders said the market shrugged off news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

"We were not affected, but it will likely be Hong Kong which will revert back to China and Taiwan which is scared of China's military might that might be affected," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
The main index finished 5.09 points lower, or 0.15 percent, at 3,310.43 points.
Traders said the market was largely indifferent to the death of 93-year old Deng Xiaoping.

"I don't think the effect in the region would be too serious as he (Deng) has been out of touch for sometime although he remained a symbolic leader. The loss is not as significant than if he was at the helm of his political career," said Saturninio Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
Diversified's Garcia said the death of the Chinese leader may even be an advantage for the Philippines as fund managers may feel safer investing in a country with less political uncertainty.
On Thursday, only the commercial-industrial and oil sub-indices were up at the session's close. There were 66 decliners and 64 gainers with 70 issues unchanged.

Volume was heavy at 55.8 billion shares valued at 4.8 billion pesos. Although thirdliners took the centrestage, blue chip San Miguel Corp A was up by 50 centavos to 55 pesos while PLDT gained 15 pesos to close at 1,575 pesos.
Rudsend Alpay of Lippo Securities said thirdliners will continue to grab attention on Friday, but next week investors were likely to revert back to blue chips.
